d.title: One number, and its sign is the whole intuition
d.caption: **Read the middle column and the dot product stops being a formula.** It is positive when two vectors broadly agree, exactly zero when they are perpendicular, and negative when they oppose — and the size says how strongly. The first row is computed both ways in the lesson and gives 24 either way: **3×4 + 4×3, or 5 × 5 × cos 16.26°.** That is why one operation serves both similarity search and projection, and why a neuron is a dot product: *how much does this input agree with what I am looking for?*

d.title: Two measurements, four dimensions, and your 2-D intuition expiring
d.caption: **Both columns are measured in the lesson, and both say the same thing: there is simply too much room.** In two dimensions two random directions overlap a lot (mean |cos| 0.637) and the furthest point is 38 times further than the nearest. In a thousand dimensions every pair of random vectors is effectively perpendicular, and **the furthest point is only 30% further away than the nearest one** — at which point “nearest neighbour” has stopped ranking anything. This is the curse of dimensionality, in two numbers.

d.title: Set the scale factor to zero, and the definition forbids translation
d.caption: **This is a two-line proof with a large consequence.** Homogeneity says f(kv) = k f(v); put k = 0 and you get f(0) = 0, so *every* matrix sends the origin to the origin. Which means the most ordinary transformation there is — sliding something sideways — is not linear, and no 2×2 matrix can do it. **The repair is to add a coordinate that is always 1**, which turns a translation into a shear one dimension up: homogeneous coordinates, the reason graphics uses 4×4 matrices for 3-D, and the reason a layer is Wx + b rather than Wx.

nodes.label: Additivity and homogeneity
nodes.sub: the two rules that define linear

nodes.label: So the origin can never move
Translation is therefore NOT linear
nodes.sub: nor is squaring, nor an activation

nodes.label: Add a coordinate that is always 1
nodes.sub: a shift becomes a shear one dim up

nodes.label: Which is why a layer is Wx + b
nodes.sub: the bias is the extra column

d.title: The row-times-column rule is forced, and the shape rule falls out of it
d.caption: **Nothing about matrix multiplication was chosen for convenience.** Applying B then A has to be the same as applying the single matrix AB — that is what composition means — and row-against-column is the only definition that delivers it. The shape rule is the same fact restated: **B's output lives in the space A takes as input, so the inner dimensions must match.** Which makes a shape error a type error rather than an arithmetic one: you are feeding a function something from the wrong space.

nodes.label: Only one rule satisfies it

nodes.label: Because B outputs into A's input space
nodes.sub: the shared k is that space

nodes.label: So a shape error is a TYPE error
nodes.sub: the wrong space, not bad arithmetic

d.title: Four numbers from one covariance matrix, and PCA is already finished
d.caption: **Every quantity PCA reports is in this table, computed before PCA is mentioned.** The eigenvalues *are* the variances along their own directions, so dividing them by their sum gives the explained-variance ratio — not a separate idea bolted on, just arithmetic. **And the trace is conserved: 1.785 before, 1.785 after.** The eigendecomposition redistributes the total spread into independent directions; it never creates or destroys any. Here one direction holds 96% of it, which is what “the data is really one-dimensional” means.

d.title: An inverse for matrices that do not have one
d.caption: **The construction is one idea: invert what you can and leave alone what you cannot.** Transpose the factorisation and reciprocate the non-zero singular values. What comes back depends on the shape of the problem, and in both cases it is the sensible answer rather than an error. **Step four is the one that bites in practice** — a singular value of 1e-16 is almost certainly noise, and reciprocating it multiplies that noise by 1e+16, so everything below a tolerance is treated as zero instead.

items.label: Factorise, then reciprocate
items.desc: A = U S V-transpose, so A-plus = V S-inverse U-transpose, inverting only the singular values that are not near zero

items.label: More equations than unknowns
items.desc: overdetermined, usually no exact solution: A-plus b returns the least-squares answer, the closest reachable point

items.label: More unknowns than equations
items.desc: underdetermined, infinitely many solutions: A-plus b returns the shortest one, the minimum-norm answer

items.label: Below the tolerance, treat as zero
items.desc: pinv discards singular values under rcond times the largest; inverting 1e-16 would amplify noise by 1e+16

d.title: 99.75% of the variance, and none of the signal
d.caption: **Two columns: one loud and meaningless, one quiet and decisive.** PCA has never seen the labels, so it ranks by spread and puts the noise first. Keep one component “retaining 99.75% of the information” and you have thrown away the only column that predicts anything — **correlation with the target drops from 0.79 to roughly zero.** This is the whole warning about PCA in one measurement: explained variance is explained *variance*, not explained target. If the reduction must respect the label, use a method that sees it.
